about: Findings review raised as blockers that a person called wrong or silly. Each must never block again, whatever a lens or skeptic says about it. Copied from the review markers on the pull requests named.

cases.why: Both true, both test gaps: the PR worked and QA passed on its preview. The user: a BS blocker.

finding.claim: The removal check can't fail on the flag part. It removes the flagged row itself (pair[1]), and `hop` is a locator inside that row, so once `row` has count 0, `hop` has count 0 by construction.
finding.evidence: tests/agenda.spec.js:84-86 removes the flagged row and then asserts the flag is gone
finding.how: an attendee removes a session whose partner stays on the page
finding.harm: a stale clash flag would go unnoticed by the suite

cases.why: True, a test gap: the seeded Jonas has no conflicts, so the loop never runs. Not something a person hits.

finding.claim: The only browser check for clashes never runs. It loops over Jonas's server-side `conflicts`, and the seeded Jonas has none.
finding.evidence: GET /api/users/1/schedule returned conflicts: [] on all four days
finding.harm: a broken clash flag would pass the suite

cases.why: A stale line in a rule file: fixed on the branch by respond, never a reason to hold back working code. The user called it silly.

finding.claim: The UI rule file still says My Agenda is a placeholder. This PR replaced the placeholder, and CLAUDE.md was updated to match, but this file was not.
finding.evidence: .claude/rules/ui.md:74 reads 'My Agenda is a coming-soon placeholder'
finding.how: the next agent reads the rule file
finding.harm: it may treat My Agenda as unbuilt

control.why: A real blocker (a stranger's fork PR got the factory's write token used on its behalf). The policy must still let a demonstrated, certain one through.

finding.claim: Code from a fork's pull request runs inside a sandbox whose network proxy adds the factory's GitHub token to every api.github.com request.
finding.evidence: a fork PR webhook payload started review; the sandbox's curl to api.github.com/user returned the factory account
finding.how: anyone opens a pull request from a fork
finding.harm: their code acts on the repository with the factory's write token
